history.summary: Built in 1772 AD by Gopalrao Jagannath Tambwekar, a shroff of the Peshwa's court at Poona; Indo-Islamic style with 8 domes and 24 turrets, the central dome reaching ~27 m (90 ft) with a golden kalash. Deity Ranchhodraiji (Krishna, 'he who left the battlefield') is said to have been brought from Dwarka by the devotee Bodana/Bholanath (legend). The throne was gifted by the Gaekwad of Baroda. Fort-wall complex on the Gomti lake in Dakor's main bazaar; unique custom - only women may offer food and flowers to the Lord. Designated one of six major Gujarat pilgrimage sites under the Yatradham Vikas Board. DUPLICATE ROW: CSV seq 304 ('Shri Ranchhodrai Dakor Temple, Godhra') refers to the SAME real temple - towns in both files corrected to Dakor; Dakor is in Kheda district, not Anand or Godhra.

name: Shree Ranchhodraiji Temple (Dakor)
town_description: Dakor is a pilgrimage town in Kheda district, Gujarat, about 30 km from Anand, set on the banks of the Gomti lake. It is one of six officially developed major pilgrimage centres in Gujarat (Yatradham Vikas Board) and is famous for the Ranchhodraiji Temple.

travel.airport: Vadodara International Airport (~61 km; some sources say ~78 km)
travel.road: Dakor GSRTC bus stand (~1 km); well connected by road to Nadiad, Anand, Ahmedabad, Vadodara

visitor_information.best_time: November-February; Janmashtami is the grandest festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Darshan ~6:45 AM-12:00 PM and ~4:15 PM-7:30 PM; closed 12:00-4:00 PM (times vary on festivals - verify)
